cards.name: Paste
cards.summary: Pastes the clipboard into the active document. Artwork lands centred in the current document window, not at the coordinates it was copied from, on the active layer (or its original layer when Paste Remembers Layers is on in the Layers panel menu). With the Type cursor inside text it inserts the copied text at the cursor.
use_for: bringing a copied logo or icon into a layout to place by eye
moving artwork between two open documents
pasting vector art copied from another app (what arrives depends on Clipboard Handling preferences)
avoid: artwork that must keep its exact position: use Paste in Place (Shift+Ctrl+V) or Paste in Front (Ctrl+F)
styled text from Word or a web page that should take the destination's styling: use Paste without Formatting (Alt+Ctrl+V)
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("paste") (id paired by shortcut, not confirmed by execution). DOM: app.paste() (harvested Application member).

cards.name: Paste in Back
cards.summary: Pastes the clipboard at the copied artwork's original position, directly behind the selected object in the stacking order and in that object's layer; with nothing selected it goes to the bottom of the active layer. The page looks unchanged until the copy is moved or recolored.
use_for: an offset drop shadow or thick outline behind a shape: copy, Paste in Back, recolor and nudge
putting a background plate directly behind a selected logo without reordering layers
a double-stroke effect from an exact duplicate underneath
avoid: pasting into another document whose artboards sit elsewhere: the copy keeps document coordinates and can land off the artboard; use Paste in Place for artboard-relative placement
outlines that must stay editable as one object: add a second stroke in the Appearance panel instead of a pasted copy
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("pasteBack") (id paired by shortcut, not confirmed by execution). Same result without the clipboard (unverified): item.duplicate(item, ElementPlacement.PLACEAFTER) puts the copy directly behind the original.

cards.name: Paste in Front
cards.summary: Pastes the clipboard at the copied artwork's original position, directly in front of the selected object in the stacking order and in that object's layer; with nothing selected it goes to the top of the active layer. The copy sits exactly over the original.
use_for: a highlight or texture layer over a shape: copy, Paste in Front, then recolor, change blend mode or opacity
keeping an untouched original underneath before a destructive Pathfinder or Offset Path edit
an exact copy on top to use as a clipping path or opacity mask
avoid: pasting into another document whose artboards sit elsewhere: the copy keeps document coordinates; use Paste in Place
many stacked copies for a simple shadow or highlight: an extra fill or stroke in the Appearance panel stays editable
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("pasteFront") (id paired by shortcut, not confirmed by execution). Same result without the clipboard (unverified): item.duplicate(item, ElementPlacement.PLACEBEFORE) puts the copy directly in front of the original.

cards.name: Paste in Place
cards.summary: Pastes the clipboard onto the active artboard at the same position the artwork had on the artboard it was copied from, on the active layer. Works across artboards and documents, so art lands at matching coordinates.
use_for: moving a header, footer or logo to the same spot on another artboard or document
copying artwork between same-size documents without re-aligning
keeping registration when splitting a design across files
avoid: putting the same element on every artboard at once: use Paste on All Artboards
placing the copy just above or below a particular object: use Paste in Front or Paste in Back
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("pasteInPlace") (id paired by shortcut, not confirmed by execution). No direct DOM call; same result (unverified): app.paste(), then set the pasted items' position from the saved artboard-relative coordinates.

review.changes: summary: dropped the unsourced 'top of the active layer' stacking claim

cards.name: Paste on All Artboards
cards.summary: Pastes one copy of the clipboard onto every artboard in the document, each at the same position relative to its artboard as the original had on the artboard it was copied from. The copies are independent objects.
use_for: page numbers, folios, logos or footers on every page of a multi-artboard brochure or deck
a watermark or corner mark across all size variants of a social campaign
a shared background element on every artboard
avoid: artboards of different sizes: the offset is repeated as-is, so art can sit off-centre or past the edge on smaller artboards; check each one
elements you will edit later in one go: the copies do not stay linked; make the element a Symbol first so one edit updates every instance
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("pasteInAllArtboard") (id paired by shortcut, not confirmed by execution). Same result without the clipboard (unverified): loop over doc.artboards, duplicate the item and translate it by each artboardRect's offset.

cards.name: Paste without Formatting
cards.summary: Pastes copied text as plain text, dropping the source's character and paragraph formatting, so inside a text frame the words take the formatting at the insertion point. It is meant for text; its behavior with no text cursor active was not checked.
use_for: dropping copy from Word, a web page or an email into a styled headline or body frame
replacing placeholder text in a template without breaking its type styles
avoid: when the source's bold, italics or colors must survive: use Paste
non-text artwork: this command is for text
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("pasteWithoutFormatting") (id paired by shortcut, not confirmed by execution). Same result without the clipboard (unverified): set textFrame.textRange.contents to the plain string, which keeps the frame's existing formatting.

cards.name: Perspective Grid Presets...
cards.summary: Opens the Perspective Grid Presets dialog, where saved perspective-grid setups are created, edited, deleted, imported and exported. It changes no artwork; it manages the presets that View > Perspective Grid applies.
cards.how: The list holds the built-in [1P-Normal View], [2P-Normal View] and [3P-Normal View] plus your own, with New, Edit, Delete, Import and Export. A preset sets (fields from memory, not harvested) the grid type (one, two or three point), units, scale, gridline spacing, viewing angle, viewing distance, horizon height, the third vanishing point (3P only), and the color and opacity of the left, right and horizontal grid planes.
use_for: a reusable 2-point grid for packaging mock-ups or architectural sketches
sharing a studio's standard perspective grid between documents or machines (Export / Import)
a grid with a fixed horizon height and scale for a series of illustrations
avoid: just switching a grid on for one drawing: View > Perspective Grid > Show Grid (Shift+Ctrl+I) and drag its widgets
giving finished flat art a quick tilt: Free Distort or the Free Transform tool's Perspective Distort is faster than redrawing on a grid
cards.script_api: No executeMenuCommand id in the harvest; the dialog runs only by its menu path / Win32 command 2147484343. Harvested Document methods cover part of its job: doc.importPerspectiveGridPreset(fileSpec[, presetName]) loads one named preset or all from a file, doc.exportPerspectiveGridPreset(file) saves all presets to a file, doc.selectPerspectivePreset(presetName) applies a preset to the document's grid. Creating, editing or deleting a preset has no DOM call.

review.changes: script_api: selectPerspectivePreset takes one argument (presetName), not (gridType, presetName), and the signatures are harvested, not unverified; scriptable no -> partial since harvested Document methods import, export and select presets; how: marked the preset fields as from memory

cards.name: Appearance of Black...
cards.summary: Opens Preferences at Appearance of Black, which decides whether pure black (K ink only) is shown and output as true flat black (Accurately) or as a deep rich black (as Rich Black), on screen and when printing to non-PostScript printers or exporting to RGB formats. It changes how black looks, not the color values in the file.
cards.how: On Screen: Display All Blacks Accurately or Display All Blacks as Rich Black. Printing / Exporting: Output All Blacks Accurately or Output All Blacks as Rich Black. The pane shows a sample of the difference.
use_for: previewing how flat a CMYK piece's pure-K text or background will print compared with a rich black
making pure-K areas look deep black in PNG or JPEG exports for screen
spotting large black areas that should be built as rich black before sending to print
avoid: fixing the ink in a print file: the preference changes no color values; set the swatch to a rich black build, and keep small black text pure K (Edit Colors > Overprint Black)
judging press output: a PDF for commercial print carries the real CMYK values whatever this pane says
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("BlackPref") opens the dialog (id paired by keyboard-shortcuts dialog alignment, not confirmed by execution). Without the dialog it would be app.preferences.setIntegerPreference(<key>, n); the preference key is not known (unverified).

review.changes: summary / use_for / avoid: replaced the unharvested '100% K' / '100K' numbers with 'pure K'

cards.name: Clipboard Handling...
cards.summary: Opens Preferences at Clipboard Handling, which sets what Illustrator puts on the clipboard when you copy (formats such as PDF, AICB and SVG code) and how text pasted from other apps is treated. It decides how art and text survive a copy to or from Photoshop, InDesign, Office or a code editor.
cards.how: On copy: PDF (keeps transparency and appearance), AICB without transparency support with Preserve Paths or Preserve Appearance and Overprints, and an option to include SVG code so a copy pastes as SVG markup into a text or code editor. On paste: whether text from other apps keeps or drops its formatting. Exact labels in 30.2 were not harvested.
use_for: pasting editable vector paths instead of a flattened picture into Photoshop or After Effects
copying an icon straight to SVG markup for a web developer
making text from Word or the web always paste plain into layouts
avoid: a one-off plain-text paste: Paste without Formatting (Alt+Ctrl+V) leaves the global setting alone
large or complex artwork exchange: a saved or exported file (AI, PDF, SVG) is more reliable than the clipboard
cards.script_api: No executeMenuCommand id in the harvest; run it by its menu path / Win32 command 2147484285. Object model (unverified): app.preferences.setBooleanPreference(<clipboard key>, value); the keys are not known.

troubleshooting touch or pen input that misbehaves only in Illustrator
avoid: any change to the artwork: the pane only affects input behavior

cards.name: Hyphenation...
cards.summary: Opens Preferences at Hyphenation: the default language used for hyphenation and an exceptions list of words with your own break points or words that must never be split. It sets rules only; whether a paragraph hyphenates at all is switched in the Paragraph panel.

cards.name: Performance...
cards.summary: Opens Preferences at Performance: GPU Performance (drawing with the graphics card, with Animated Zoom), Real-Time Drawing and Editing, and Undo Counts, the number of undo steps Illustrator keeps.
cards.how: GPU Performance on renders the canvas on the graphics card (faster zoom, pan and preview); Animated Zoom smooths Zoom-tool drags; Real-Time Drawing and Editing redraws art live while dragging; Undo Counts trades memory for more history steps. The exact list in 30.2 was not harvested.
use_for: switching GPU Performance off when the canvas shows render artifacts, flicker or driver crashes
more undo steps for exploratory work on a machine with plenty of RAM
faster redraw on dense illustrations
avoid: export or print problems: GPU Performance only affects on-screen drawing
very high undo counts on low-RAM machines: memory use rises
